title: March to the Park!
description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Mark your calendars! Bring the kids! Join us on June 21st @ 10:30am for our March to the Park! from the Tuscarawas Co Courthouse to Tuscora Park (one mile). Join us afterwards for a potluck. Together with the League of Women Voters Tuscarawas County, we are collecting monetary donations for Jack’s House of Hope. 

Departure time: 10:45am! Bring your own signs to this event.

Signs

For this event, please bring your own signs. They can be on wood sticks such as tomatoe posts for ease of carrying. Make your message clear: Federal, state, and local issues of concern to you, your family, the community…there are just so many issues my head would explode if I wrote them all down. Pre-made signs will not be available for this event.

Monetary Donations

Together with the League of Women Voters of Tusc County, we are asking marchers to make a monetary donation of any amount for Jack’s House of Hope. Monetary donations for Jack’s House of Hope will be collected at Tuscora Park. Amanda Fontana, Friends of the Homeless of Tuscarawas County Board of Directors' Secretary will speak about the importance of our local shelter.

March, Eat, Chat, Play!

Our event is from 10:30am-12:30pm. We will march to Tuscora Park from the Tuscarawas County Courthouse and then share a covered dish and/or just bring something for yourself/your family, your own paper products/utensils, snacks to share, and good conversation with those joining us. If you bring something to share, please be mindful of allergies. An index card with a list of ingredients taped to the container would be appreciated. Label containers with your name if you want them back! Jenn Schrock will oversee the food/refreshments while we march.

Half of a covered pavilion near the bocce courts has been reserved for this event. Blankets and chairs can be dropped off beforehand. Marchers can carpool back to the Tusc Co Courthouse to then walk to the park (10:45am). For those that do not have a way back to the courthouse to march, Alicia Hall will help transport people to the courthouse BEFORE the march once they drop off their items at the park.

Remember: Bring your own signs to this event!

Kids can play on the playground equipment. Park rides and Putt-Putt golf open at NOON. See pricing at www.tuscorapark.com/park-info-contact.

We’ll take a group picture!

Helpers

We need helpers at the park to remain with the food, etc. until the marchers arrive. We also need help along the route, guiding marchers as they cross side streets. We don’t block traffic, we hold marchers on the sidewalk while traffic makes their turn left or right onto North Broadway. Let us know if you’re interested in helping.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

description:
Please join us for an organizing zoom call ahead of our third town hall leg in Eastern Idaho. On June 18th, we’ll be meeting at 5:30pm to discuss the logistics of pulling off a successful round of town halls to help inform the public of the dangers of vouchers and the need for people to get involved in this important fight.

During the 2025 legislative session, Idaho lawmakers passed House Bill 93 and enacted a $50 million school-voucher program. For the first time in state history, Idaho tax dollars will be used to subsidize the cost of tuition for private-school families. 

The special-interest groups promoting vouchers have made clear that the $50 million program is only the beginning. During next year’s legislative session, they intend to remove the $50-million cap and expand the program to all private-school families, including the wealthy, at an estimated cost of $339 million per year.
 
Such a massive expansion of vouchers would bankrupt Idaho and drain millions from public schools. For the benefit of a small number of private-school families, it would defund the public education system that serves 94% of Idaho’s kids. 

It may be inevitable that the legislature tries to expand House Bill 93, but it is not inevitable that they will succeed. To stop this attack on public schools, we need to get organized. Please sign up if you can make it and we hope to see you soon!

description:
## South Mountain Democrats Banned Book Club - June

Join us for this month’s gathering of the Banned Book Club as we dive into The Handmaid’s Tale by Margaret Atwood.

Originally published in 1985, The Handmaid’s Tale is a dystopian novel that explores themes of authoritarianism, reproductive rights, and resistance in a chillingly patriarchal society. Atwood’s work has been both critically acclaimed and frequently challenged, with bans citing its political content, sexual themes, and critique of religious extremism.

### Come for the conversation — stay for the community. All are welcome.

title: Jews for Shahana Get Out the Vote Canvassing!
description:
Join #TeamShahana for our Jews for Shahana Get Out the Vote event on Sunday, June 15th at 12:00pm! Early voting starts on the 14th, so we need as much help as we can get moving people to the polls to cast early ballots for Shahana! 

Already, Jewish members of our community have showed up in force to support Shahana Hanif, whether it's been through collective days of action or regular weeknight canvassing. Now more than ever, we need your help to keep Shahana in city hall by getting our constituents to the polls!

The only way to re-elect Councilmember Shahana Hanif is through the work of volunteers like yourself. We will provide training and resources day of to all in attendance.

Sign up to help us win today!
